text:
The Hockey Writers called it "Stanley Cup Confidence," and Andrei Svechnikov's start does look like a champion's. He has 23 points (13 goals) in 23 games, ten on the power play, and a four-game, seven-point streak in mid-November that CBS Sports noted.

The process is real. He has 10.49 expected goals (the quality of his chances), well above his rate last season, and Carolina takes 62% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows why he matters beyond scoring: he carried the puck in on 56% of his entries last season and ranked in the 86th percentile among forwards in primary shot assists.

The finishing is the part to hold loosely. He has 13 goals on 10.5 expected, shooting 19% against 15% last season, a rate that rarely lasts. Evolving-Hockey's read on last season was the mirror image: 1.5 expected wins against 0.4 actual, as the chances outran the goals. It also flagged a cost, with chances against rising when he plays. Watch the shot volume and the carries; that is the part he controls.
